title: cancelled_recurring-definition
text: Cancelled recurring: definition and qualifying conditions. A recurring charge (subscription, membership, plan, auto-renewal, standing card authority) was billed after the cardholder cancelled, after the merchant confirmed the cancellation, or after the cardholder withdrew permission for future charges. Qualifying conditions: (1) a recurring arrangement the cardholder had set up; (2) cancellation or revoked consent before the disputed billing date; (3) the merchant billed again. Network references: Visa 13.2, Mastercard 4841.

title: cancelled_recurring-evidence
text: Cancelled recurring: evidence and exclusions. Evidence: the cancellation confirmation or its date, a screenshot of the closed account, the renewal charge date. Exclusions: a one-off purchase is not recurring; a renewal the cardholder never tried to cancel is not this category; recurring charges from a merchant the cardholder never had an account with are unauthorised. A renewal after cancellation stays in this category when the merchant promised a refund (R3) or when the cardholder calls it a duplicate (R10).

title: cancelled_recurring-precedent-1
text: Precedent: meal-kit plan cancelled in the app. A cardholder cancelled a meal-kit plan in the app on 28 May and received a confirmation email. A ₹2,999 charge for the June box posted on 1 June. Decision: cancelled_recurring.

title: cancelled_recurring-precedent-2
text: Precedent: annual cloud-storage renewal with a refund promise. A cardholder cancelled a cloud-storage plan, the merchant billed the annual renewal anyway, and support promised to refund it within a week, which never happened. Decision: cancelled_recurring. Recurring billing after cancellation takes precedence over credit_not_processed (R3).

title: credit_not_processed-definition
text: Credit not processed: definition and qualifying conditions. The merchant acknowledged that money is owed back and the credit did not arrive, or arrived short. Qualifying conditions: (1) a merchant acknowledgement: refund confirmation or reference, accepted return, cancellation with refund wording, a promise in chat or email; (2) a reasonable time has passed since the acknowledgement, typically 7 to 15 business days; (3) no credit, or a partial credit (R8). Network references: Visa 13.6, Mastercard 4853.

title: credit_not_processed-evidence
text: Credit not processed: evidence and exclusions. Evidence: the refund confirmation, return tracking showing delivery to the merchant, a cancellation confirmation that mentions a refund, a credit slip. Exclusions: the merchant never agreed to refund (classify the underlying problem instead: product_quality, product_not_received or service_not_rendered); recurring billing after cancellation takes precedence even when a refund was promised (cancelled_recurring, R3).

title: credit_not_processed-precedent-1
text: Precedent: sofa returned, refund initiated, nothing posted. A cardholder returned a sofa; the courier's proof of delivery shows the retailer's warehouse received it on 2 March, and the retailer emailed "refund initiated". By 10 April no credit had posted. Decision: credit_not_processed.

title: credit_not_processed-precedent-2
text: Precedent: airline refunded half. After cancelling a flight, an airline's app showed "refund processed: ₹18,200", but only ₹9,100 reached the card. Decision: credit_not_processed. A short credit is still a credit not processed (R8), and the refund acknowledgement outranks service_not_rendered (R2).

title: duplicate_processing-definition
text: Duplicate processing: definition and qualifying conditions. A single purchase was charged more than once, or the cardholder paid by another method and the card was charged as well (R4). Qualifying conditions: (1) one purchase: one order, booking, bill or invoice; (2) two or more settled charges for it, usually the same amount close together in time, or proof of a second payment by other means; (3) the cardholder recognises the merchant. Network references: Visa 12.6.1 and 12.6.2, Mastercard 4834.

title: duplicate_processing-evidence
text: Duplicate processing: evidence and exclusions. Evidence: both statement lines, a single receipt or order number, proof of the other payment (cash receipt, transfer reference). Exclusions: a pending authorisation hold that drops off; two genuine separate purchases; a recurring charge after cancellation that the cardholder calls a "double charge" (cancelled_recurring, R10); one charge for more than the agreed price, or an extra fee posted as a separate line (incorrect_amount); two charges from a merchant the cardholder does not recognise (unauthorised).

title: duplicate_processing-precedent-1
text: Precedent: fuel terminal timeout. At a fuel station the card terminal timed out and the attendant re-ran the card. Both ₹3,450 charges settled two minutes apart for a single fill-up. Decision: duplicate_processing.

title: duplicate_processing-precedent-2
text: Precedent: plumber paid by transfer and by card. A cardholder paid a plumber's invoice by bank transfer, and the plumber also charged the card kept on file for the same invoice. Decision: duplicate_processing (paid by other means, R4), not incorrect_amount and not unauthorised.

title: incorrect_amount-definition
text: Incorrect amount: definition and qualifying conditions. The cardholder agreed to the purchase but was charged more than the agreed price: an overcharge, an undisclosed fee, an altered tip, extra nights or days, the wrong quantity, or a quote that was exceeded. Qualifying conditions: (1) the cardholder recognises and agreed to the transaction; (2) there is an agreed price, such as a receipt, quote, menu, meter or booking; (3) the charged amount is higher than that price. Network references: Visa 12.5, Mastercard 4831.

title: incorrect_amount-evidence
text: Incorrect amount: evidence and exclusions. Evidence: the receipt or quote, the statement amount, the booking terms showing which fees were disclosed. Exclusions: the price was right but the mechanics were wrong, such as currency, wrong card or late posting (processing_error, R5); one purchase charged twice for the full amount each time (duplicate_processing); a merchant the cardholder does not recognise (unauthorised); a refund smaller than promised (credit_not_processed, R8).

title: incorrect_amount-precedent-1
text: Precedent: restaurant tip altered. A restaurant bill was ₹2,400 and the cardholder wrote a ₹200 tip on the slip, but the statement shows ₹3,400. Decision: incorrect_amount (altered tip).

title: incorrect_amount-precedent-2
text: Precedent: undisclosed cleaning fee at a car-rental desk. A car-rental desk added ₹4,500 for "premium cleaning", a fee that was not in the booking terms. Decision: incorrect_amount, because an undisclosed fee exceeds the agreed price (R5).

title: R1 Recognition beats wording
text: If the cardholder recognises the merchant or admits making the purchase, the dispute is not unauthorised, even when they write "fraud", "unauthorised" or "I didn't authorise this". Words like these often mean "I didn't agree to what happened", not "it wasn't me". Classify by what went wrong with the recognised purchase: the amount, the delivery, the condition, the renewal, or the processing.

title: R2 An acknowledged refund that never arrived is credit not processed
text: If the merchant agreed to refund, issued a refund confirmation or reference, accepted a return, or cancelled an order or booking while promising the money back, and the credit did not arrive, label credit_not_processed. This holds even when the original problem was quality, non-delivery or a cancelled service: once the merchant has acknowledged the debt, the dispute is about the missing credit. Exception: recurring billing after cancellation (R3).

title: R3 Billing after cancelling a recurring plan is cancelled recurring
text: A subscription, membership, plan or auto-renewal charge taken after the cardholder cancelled, or after the merchant confirmed the cancellation, is cancelled_recurring. It stays cancelled_recurring even if the merchant later promised to refund that charge, and even if the renewal came through at a different price. The root cause is the cancellation not being honoured.

title: R4 Paid by other means counts as duplicate processing
text: If the cardholder paid for the same purchase by another method (cash, cash on delivery, another card, bank transfer, UPI, voucher) and the card was charged as well, label duplicate_processing. This includes a terminal that showed a decline, after which the cardholder paid with a different card and both were charged. Without a second payment, a charge after a decline is processing_error (R5).

title: R5 Price wrong versus mechanics wrong
text: Compare what was charged with what was agreed. If the agreed price itself was exceeded (overcharge, undisclosed fee, altered tip, extra nights, wrong quantity, a quote that was exceeded) label incorrect_amount. If the agreed price was right but the processing was wrong (wrong currency, a conversion the cardholder declined, the wrong card or account, a charge after a decline, posting months late, a refund processed as a charge) label processing_error. A merchant blaming "currency conversion" when no foreign currency was involved is still incorrect_amount.

title: R6 Goods versus services
text: Physical goods and digital goods (downloads, licence keys, gift cards and e-gift cards, in-game items) that never arrived are product_not_received. Experiences, bookings, appointments, travel, events, classes, online courses, memberships to a venue, installations, repairs and labour that did not happen are service_not_rendered. When a purchase bundles both, classify by the part the cardholder actually paid for and did not get.

title: R7 Wrong or broken is quality, missing is not received
text: A delivered item that is damaged, defective, counterfeit, used when sold as new, the wrong item, the wrong size or model, or materially different from its description is product_quality. Items missing from a delivery, or a parcel marked delivered that never reached the cardholder, are product_not_received.

title: R8 A short refund is still credit not processed
text: If the merchant refunded less than the amount it agreed to refund, label credit_not_processed (a partial credit), not incorrect_amount. Incorrect_amount is about the original charge exceeding the agreed price, not about the size of a refund.

title: R9 A failed service with no refund promise is service not rendered
text: If the merchant cancelled or failed to provide a service and has not agreed to refund, label service_not_rendered. Silence, a closed website or a shut-down company is not a refund agreement. Contrast R2: the same cancelled event becomes credit_not_processed once the organiser promises a refund that never comes.

title: R10 Classify by the facts, not the stated reason
text: Cardholders often pick the wrong reason. When the reason they name ("duplicate", "item not received", "wrong amount", "fraud") contradicts the facts they describe, the facts decide. Example: a cardholder files "item not received" for a parcel they received and sent back with the seller's approval; the facts describe a refund that never arrived, so the label is credit_not_processed.

title: processing_error-definition
text: Processing error: definition and qualifying conditions. The price was right but the transaction was processed wrongly: the wrong currency or a conversion the cardholder declined, posted to the wrong card or account, charged although the terminal showed a decline, posted months after the purchase (late presentment), or a refund processed as a charge. Qualifying conditions: (1) the cardholder agreed to the purchase and its price; (2) a technical or processing fault changed how it was charged. Network references: Visa 12.1 to 12.4 and 12.7, Mastercard 4834.

title: processing_error-evidence
text: Processing error: evidence and exclusions. Evidence: the receipt in the original currency, the terminal's decline slip, the purchase date versus the posting date, statements from both cards involved. Exclusions: a higher price than agreed (incorrect_amount, R5); a decline followed by payment with another method, after which both were charged (duplicate_processing, R4); a refund that never arrived (credit_not_processed).

title: processing_error-precedent-1
text: Precedent: Dubai hotel converted to rupees. A hotel in Dubai agreed a room rate in dirhams but charged the card in rupees, at a conversion rate the cardholder had declined on the terminal. Decision: processing_error (unrequested conversion, R5).

title: processing_error-precedent-2
text: Precedent: refund keyed as a sale. At an electronics store a ₹1,500 refund was keyed as a ₹1,500 sale, so the cardholder was charged instead of credited. Decision: processing_error (incorrect transaction code).

title: product_not_received-definition
text: Product not received: definition and qualifying conditions. The cardholder paid for goods that never arrived, arrived only in part, or did not arrive by the agreed date, and the merchant has not agreed to a refund. Qualifying conditions: (1) a purchase of goods, physical or digital: downloads, licence keys, gift cards and in-game items count as goods (R6); (2) the expected delivery date has passed, or the merchant cannot show delivery to the cardholder; (3) the cardholder did not receive the goods, or some items were missing (R7). Network references: Visa 13.1, Mastercard 4855.

title: product_not_received-evidence
text: Product not received: evidence and exclusions. Evidence: the order confirmation with the promised date, tracking that never shows delivery or shows delivery to the wrong place, unanswered messages to the merchant. Exclusions: goods that arrived damaged, wrong or different from the description (product_quality, R7); a booking or service that did not happen (service_not_rendered, R6); a merchant that agreed to refund and did not pay (credit_not_processed, R2).

title: product_not_received-precedent-1
text: Precedent: smartwatch stuck at label created. A cardholder bought a smartwatch with an estimated delivery date of 5 June. Tracking stayed at "label created" from 1 June, and the seller stopped replying. Decision: product_not_received.

title: product_not_received-precedent-2
text: Precedent: game licence key never emailed. A cardholder bought a licence key for a video game; the key was never emailed and the store's support ticket stayed unanswered. Decision: product_not_received, because digital goods count as goods (R6).

title: product_quality-definition
text: Product quality: definition and qualifying conditions. The goods arrived but were damaged, defective, counterfeit, used when sold as new, the wrong item, size or model, or materially different from the description, and the merchant has not agreed to a refund. Qualifying conditions: (1) the cardholder received the goods; (2) a specific defect or mismatch with the description or order; (3) the cardholder tried to resolve it, or the merchant refused a return. Network references: Visa 13.3 and 13.4, Mastercard 4853.

title: product_quality-evidence
text: Product quality: evidence and exclusions. Evidence: photos, the original listing, an expert opinion for counterfeits, the merchant's refusal of a return. Exclusions: the item never arrived or parts of the order are missing (product_not_received, R7); the merchant accepted a return or promised a refund that never came (credit_not_processed, R2); a merchant that only offered to "look into it" has not agreed a refund, so the dispute stays product_quality; changing one's mind without any defect does not qualify.

title: product_quality-precedent-1
text: Precedent: wool coat that was polyester. A cardholder ordered a coat listed as 100% wool; the sewn-in label said 80% polyester. The seller refused a return, citing a final-sale policy. Decision: product_quality (not as described).

title: product_quality-precedent-2
text: Precedent: bicycle with a bent wheel. A bicycle arrived with a bent rear wheel although the courier's photo showed an intact box. The merchant denied the claim. Decision: product_quality. The goods were received; the problem is their condition (R7).

title: service_not_rendered-definition
text: Service not rendered: definition and qualifying conditions. The cardholder paid for a service, booking, event, class, online course, installation, repair, or travel that did not take place or was not provided as agreed, and the merchant has not agreed to refund. Qualifying conditions: (1) a purchase of a service rather than goods (R6); (2) the service date has passed, or the merchant has stopped trading or cannot perform; (3) the cardholder was willing and able to receive the service. Network references: Visa 13.1 (services), Mastercard 4855.

title: service_not_rendered-evidence
text: Service not rendered: evidence and exclusions. Evidence: the booking confirmation, proof the cardholder turned up or was available, a cancellation notice from the merchant, an unreachable provider. Exclusions: goods, including digital goods (product_not_received, R6); a merchant that cancelled and promised a refund which never came (credit_not_processed, R2); a cardholder who simply did not attend.

title: service_not_rendered-precedent-1
text: Precedent: wedding photographer no-show. A cardholder prepaid ₹6,000 to a wedding photographer who never arrived on the day and stopped answering calls. Decision: service_not_rendered.

title: service_not_rendered-precedent-2
text: Precedent: bootcamp portal never unlocked. An online coding bootcamp took payment but the course portal never unlocked, and support tickets went unanswered. Decision: service_not_rendered. Course access is a service (R6), and no refund was agreed (R9).

title: unauthorised-definition
text: Unauthorised: definition and qualifying conditions. The cardholder did not make, permit or take part in the transaction. Typical causes are a lost or stolen card, card details used online without permission (card-not-present fraud), or account takeover. Qualifying conditions: (1) the cardholder does not recognise the merchant or the purchase; (2) they did not give the card or credentials to whoever used them; (3) they received no goods or services from the transaction. If the cardholder recognises the merchant and engaged with them, use another category (R1). Network references: Visa 10.4, Mastercard 4837.

title: unauthorised-evidence
text: Unauthorised: evidence and exclusions. Evidence: the cardholder's statement that they did not participate; card status (reported lost or stolen, or still in their possession); a delivery address, device or location that does not match the cardholder. Exclusions: a recognised merchant charging the wrong amount (incorrect_amount); a recognised subscription that renewed after cancellation (cancelled_recurring); repeated charges from a merchant the cardholder never dealt with are still unauthorised, not duplicate or recurring, because there was no purchase or plan of theirs to duplicate or cancel.

title: unauthorised-precedent-1
text: Precedent: three overnight charges from a Romanian electronics site. A cardholder in Pune reported three charges from an electronics web shop in Romania placed within an hour, while the card stayed in their drawer. They had never visited the site, and the orders shipped to a freight forwarder. Decision: unauthorised. The merchant was unknown, the card was not shared, and nothing was received.

title: unauthorised-precedent-2
text: Precedent: "fraud" that was a forgotten membership. A cardholder flagged a FITZONE debit as fraud. On review they had been a member and had cancelled in writing two months earlier, and the debit was the regular monthly fee. Decision: cancelled_recurring, not unauthorised. The cardholder recognised the merchant once reminded (R1), and the charge came after a cancellation (R3).
